problem: Prior VLN agents (e.g., the Seq2Seq student-forcing model of Anderson et al. and RPA) learn a single direct instruction-to-action mapping. They face three problems: little annotated data (R2R has about 21.5k instructions), low-level visuomotor actions (turn 30°, forward) that do not match the granularity of human instructions, and no mechanism for globally checking whether a chosen route actually explains the instruction. As a result they reach only about 20-25% SR in unseen environments.
motivation: Human route instructions name only a few high-level decisions and landmarks, so the follower must infer the missing details and resolve ambiguity, for example which of two bedrooms is meant or how far 'walk a bit' goes. Computational pragmatics (the Rational Speech Acts framework) shows that a listener which reasons about a speaker model can resolve such ambiguity, but it had been applied only to very simple forced-choice tasks. A learned speaker (route → instruction) can serve two purposes: it can label new routes to create training data, and it can score candidate routes by how well they explain the instruction.
key_idea: Train a seq2seq speaker P_S(d|r) alongside the seq2seq follower P_F(r|d). The speaker (a) generates synthetic instructions for 178k sampled routes as data augmentation and (b) at test time pragmatically reranks follower-generated candidate routes by P_S^λ·P_F^(1−λ). Both models operate in a panoramic action space that selects among navigable adjacent viewpoints.
insight: All three components help on their own and all three matter in the full model. Added alone to the Row-1 baseline on val-unseen (SR 19.9), pragmatic inference gives the biggest single gain (34.5), then the panoramic action space (31.2), then augmentation (24.6). Removing each from the full model (54.6 SR val-unseen) gives 35.5 without pragmatics, 39.3 without panoramic space, and 49.5 without augmentation (Table 1). Search alone is not the source of the gain: rescoring the same K=40 state-factored candidates with the follower only (λ=0) gives 43.7 vs 54.6 with the speaker (Table A.1). The best weighting is λ=0.95, i.e. almost pure speaker/RSA scoring. Gains from more candidates saturate quickly: K=5 already reaches 50.3. Speaker augmentation helps relatively more in unseen than in seen environments, and more synthetic data helps (25% of the data gives 22.8 vs 24.6 SR val-unseen with all of it, in the non-panoramic setting).
method: Follower P_F(r|d): LSTM seq2seq with attention over the encoded instruction words, outputting navigation actions sequentially; trained with student-forcing (actions sampled from the model, supervised by shortest-path actions); word embeddings initialized with GloVe.

Speaker P_S(d|r): symmetric seq2seq in which an LSTM encodes the route's visual observations and actions and an attention LSTM decoder generates the instruction word by word; trained with cross-entropy (MLE) on R2R train.

Speaker-driven data augmentation: sample M=178,000 shortest-path routes in the training environments and label them with greedy speaker decoding; train the follower on augmented + original data for 50k iterations, then fine-tune on the original human data for 20k iterations.

State-factored search for candidate routes: best-first search in which partial routes compete per environment state (location, heading, completed flag), keeping only the best-scoring route to each state and re-expanding a state if a better route to it appears; runs until K=40 routes with distinct end states have issued STOP. This yields acyclic routes and also improves the follower on its own compared with greedy decoding.
Pragmatic inference (RSA-style rescoring): choose argmax over candidates of P_S(d|r)^λ · P_F(r|d)^(1−λ), with λ=0.95 tuned on validation.

Panoramic action space: the agent sees 36 views (12 headings × 3 elevations), each encoded as ImageNet ResNet features plus [sinψ; cosψ; sinθ; cosθ]. Visual attention over the 36 views conditioned on h_{t−1} feeds the LSTM, and a bilinear score over navigable-direction encodings u_j (with a STOP vector u_0 = 0) picks the next adjacent viewpoint. A built-in mapping converts this choice into low-level turn/move actions.

setting.backbone: LSTM seq2seq follower + LSTM seq2seq speaker (trained from scratch, GloVe-initialized embeddings) on frozen ImageNet-pretrained ResNet features
setting.training_data: R2R train split (human instructions) plus 178,000 speaker-generated synthetic route–instruction pairs sampled in the R2R training environments; follower then fine-tuned on original R2R train
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views as ResNet features + heading/elevation encoding)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (choose among navigable adjacent directions or STOP), mapped to low-level turn/move by a built-in mapping
setting.privileged: none in terms of GT info. However, the headline pragmatic-inference results use test-time search over up to K=40 candidate routes, and only the single selected route is scored; the physically executed trajectory for the challenge-compliant version averages 1257.38 m.

numbers_note: The paper does not report SPL; it predates the metric. Headline results score only the route selected after search, not the physical exploration; the challenge-compliant trajectory has TL 1257.38 m. The effect of K (number of candidates) is shown only in Figure A.2; the text quotes K=5 at 50.3% SR val-unseen and greedy at 35.5%. The text cites 43.5% SR for state-factored search without pragmatics at K=1, while Table A.1 lists 43.7 for λ=0; these are slightly different settings or numbers. Test-set ablations beyond the rows above are not given.
results: On R2R the full speaker-follower model reaches 54.6% SR / 4.83 m NE on val-unseen and 53.5% SR / 4.87 m NE on test (unseen). This more than doubles the prior state of the art, RPA (24.6% val-unseen, 25.3% test), and Seq2Seq student-forcing (20.4% test). It was the top entry on the VLN Challenge leaderboard at the time. The strict single-run version keeps the same 53.49% SR but has TL 1257.38 m. Without pragmatic inference (greedy panoramic follower with augmentation), the model gets 35.5% SR on val-unseen and 35.08% on test.
limitations: Pragmatic inference needs to explore up to K=40 full candidate routes before acting. When executed physically (challenge-compliant), trajectories average 1257.38 m and OSR is inflated to 96.0%, so path efficiency is very poor. The speaker can only rank complete routes, not partial ones.
Speaker-generated instructions are noisy, so a final fine-tuning stage on the original human data is required.
The method is evaluated only on R2R with discrete nav-graph navigation. The panoramic action space relies on the simulator's navigable-direction graph and a built-in mapping to low-level control.
